context: The prompt requests automatic refresh of the statuses and mode buttons on the Active Prompt page every 2 seconds without interrupting user activities. Several implementation and UX details are ambiguous (which exact elements to refresh, whether the interval should be configurable, mechanism to use, and how to avoid interfering with user interaction). This questionnaire collects preferences to resolve these ambiguities.

questions.question-text: Which specific UI elements should be considered 'statuses and mode buttons' for the automatic refresh?

options.label: Only the status badges and mode toggle buttons in the active prompt header
options.pros: Minimal scope, lowest risk of side effects, easiest to implement and test
options.cons: May miss other status indicators elsewhere on the page that the user expects to be live

options.label: All status indicators and mode buttons across the Active Prompt page
options.pros: Comprehensive, keeps all visible statuses up-to-date
options.cons: Larger DOM updates, higher risk of interfering with active UI components or performance

options.label: Only interactive mode buttons (not passive status text/badges)
options.pros: Avoids changing passive UI that users may be reading; focuses on actionable controls
options.cons: Status visibility may lag if passive indicators are excluded

options.label: Other (please specify)
options.cons: Requires additional user input to disambiguate

questions.recommendation-rationale: Recommend limiting scope to header status badges and mode toggle buttons to minimize risk and keep refresh behavior predictable while still addressing the common need.

questions.question-text: Should the 2-second refresh interval be fixed, configurable, or adaptive?

options.label: Fixed at 2 seconds (as stated)
options.pros: Matches the prompt exactly, simple implementation
options.cons: May be too frequent for some users or environments, potential performance impact

options.label: Configurable default 2 seconds (exposed in settings)
options.pros: Flexibility for different usage contexts, user can reduce frequency to save resources
options.cons: Requires UI for settings and persistence, slightly more engineering effort

options.label: Adaptive interval (increases when idle or under load)
options.cons: More complex to implement and test; behavior may be less predictable to users

questions.recommendation-rationale: Recommend a configurable default of 2 seconds: it satisfies the prompt while allowing users or deployments to reduce frequency if needed.

questions.question-text: Which technical approach should be used to implement the refresh behavior?

options.label: Client-side polling using a lightweight setInterval and targeted partial DOM updates
options.pros: Simple to implement, works with existing REST APIs, no server changes
options.cons: Inefficient compared to push for frequent updates; may increase server requests

options.label: Server push (WebSocket/Server-Sent Events) to update only changed values
options.pros: Efficient for frequent updates, minimal extra requests, lower latency
options.cons: Requires backend support and more complex integration/testing

options.label: Hybrid: short-polling fallback to server push when supported
options.pros: Best of both worlds; graceful degradation
options.cons: Most complex to implement and test

questions.recommendation-rationale: Recommend client-side polling initially for simplicity and compatibility; consider server push in future if frequent updates and scale demand it.

questions.question-text: Should automatic refresh be suppressed or modified while the user is interacting with related UI elements (hovering, focusing, typing)?

options.label: Yes — pause or defer refresh while the user interacts with the elements
options.pros: Prevents unexpected UI changes during user interaction, reduces interruption
options.cons: May delay visible updates and cause the UI to become stale briefly

options.label: No — continue seamless background updates without visible interruption
options.pros: Keeps data freshest at all times
options.cons: Risk of UI jumps that interfere with user actions

options.label: Partial suppression — suppress only if the element is focused or a modal is open
options.cons: Slightly more complex logic to detect interaction state

questions.recommendation-rationale: Recommend partial suppression: pause updates when elements are focused or when modals are open, but allow background updates otherwise to balance UX and freshness.
